html:
The Malian Gulf tsunami struck the coasts of central Greece and the island of Euboea in the summer of 426 BCE, after a series of earthquakes.

At the town of Orobiae on Euboea the sea pulled back and then rushed in over the land, drowning part of the town. Other coastal places were flooded too. The same earthquakes made a Spartan army turn back from its yearly invasion of Attica during the Peloponnesian War.

The event matters for science as much as war. Thucydides asked why it happened and concluded that the earthquake must have caused the wave, since without it he could not see how such a thing could occur. He is the first person known to have explained a tsunami this way. Two generations earlier, Herodotus had put a flood at Potidaea down to the anger of Poseidon.

Greece is a land of earthquakes. A few decades earlier a quake had flattened Sparta, and in 373 BCE another one sank the city of Helike.
sum: The Malian Gulf tsunami struck the coasts of central Greece and the island of Euboea in the summer of 426 BCE, after a series of earthquakes.
